FL-143.label: Neo-noir as the default style, with other configurations easily uploadable.
FL-143.walk: Open a fresh install; NEO-NOIR is the style, and another configuration can be uploaded and selected.
FL-143.observed: Fresh browser default was NEO-NOIR. Uploading cobalt-seraph-plate.png created selectable PLATE 40BFC441 with all six palette checks passing; selection persisted. See before/FL-143-default.png and pressed-colorway.json.

FL-145.label: Two alternate themes derived from your reference picture (Seraph Dressed, Gold Lines) added beside the current color scheme.
FL-145.walk: Switch to Gold Lines; the interface takes on the picture's colors and the original scheme remains selectable.
FL-145.observed: Selected Gold Lines and Seraph Dressed in the real app; NEO-NOIR and uploaded plate remain selectable.

FL-146.label: The reference picture's exact colors are pulled out and applied to the Harness algorithmically in the picture's proportions, possibly by assigning colors to parts of the module templates.
FL-146.walk: Put a themed screen beside the reference picture; the same exact colors appear in the picture's proportions.
FL-146.observed: Exact sampled colors and recorded contrast repairs passed the existing deterministic extractor/validator. Live Seraph palette L1 distance 0.366642 and uploaded plate 0.386012 pass inherited 0.395 bound. This is distribution regression evidence, not pixel equality or a new aesthetic threshold.

FL-187.label: Two repos, the spine (memory) and the Harness, not a mono repo.
FL-187.walk: List the repositories; the spine and the Harness are two separate git repos.
FL-187.observed: Opened the public nocturne-harness and nocturne-memory GitHub repositories separately. Companion screenshot after/FL-187-memory-repository.png shows Memory; Git remotes and release metadata remain separate.

FL-191.label: The tools and skills Claude Code and Codex use on this machine, pinned to versioned open-source sources.
FL-191.walk: Open the tool inventory; each tool or skill lists the versioned open-source source it is pinned to.
FL-191.observed: Opened live Tools & skills: each listed tool exposes a versioned source URL. Native additions 0.1.27, pydantic-ai-harness 0.31.0 and Playwright 1.62.0. Full visible text retained in receipts/tool-inventory.txt.

FL-194.label: The Pydantic toolset and skills as the tool layer.
FL-194.walk: Open the agent's tool list in a thread; the tools come from the Pydantic toolset plus skills, not from pi.
FL-194.observed: Live thread Tools & skills lists Pydantic read/edit/write/grep/find/ls/bash and background shells with pinned upstream, plus native memory, move, browser and delegation tools; no pi toolset. See tool-inventory receipt.

FL-195.label: The feature ledger generates coverage reports and requires evidence for the rows affected by a build.
FL-195.walk: Compute the composer fix's impact with --paths and see attunement rows; push a branch touching socket.ts and observe the hook print rows and write impacted.json; observe a DONE handoff without screenshots fail CI, then verify complete evidence passes.
FL-195.observed: All 30 local ledger/rules negative and control tests passed, including missing-evidence refusal and valid evidence acceptance. A dedicated failing hosted CI push was not run in this brand packet; screenshot is live-app context only.

FL-196.label: The rules machine checks citations, frozen law, product vocabulary, seed states and packet precedents.
FL-196.walk: Remove a guard citation on a disposable branch and observe CI fail; change a frozen axiom and observe the freeze step fail; restore both and observe Rules pass. The master ADR check remains red until the owner applies the citation patch.
FL-196.observed: Current rules pass and all 30 local negative/control tests pass. Dedicated hosted guard-citation and frozen-axiom mutation runs were not performed; screenshot is live-app context only.

FL-009.label: Record files (history, transcripts) live apart from code so code can be deleted and re-downloaded without losing history.
FL-009.walk: Delete the code folder, reinstall, `nocturne up`; every thread is still there.
FL-009.observed: Public 0.1.27 code-environment deletion and reinstall restored the disposable conversation. The new 0.1.28 release install/restoration remains pending publication.

FL-069.label: The core tools every modern harness has: files, terminal, Chrome, skills, changing models, compaction (our own take), and interactions with common apps, taken from the most modular standard source.
FL-069.walk: Ask the agent to read a file, run a terminal command, open a page in the browser and use a skill; each works.
FL-069.observed: No combined read, shell, browser and skill execution was performed in this brand walk. The live provider reply and installed inventory do not prove that broader workflow.

FL-144.label: The name Nocturne and the mark: an ouroboros around the moon.
FL-144.walk: Look at the header; the Nocturne mark shows an ouroboros around the moon.
FL-144.observed: Header and served favicon show the ouroboros around the moon. The release candidate wheel contains byte-identical harness/_web/favicon.svg; receipts/packaged-icon.json. Baseline favicon was a tan H.

FL-147.label: Wizard Mode and Technomancer themes with our own glyph scripts, runes appearing and disappearing.
FL-147.walk: Switch to Wizard Mode and Technomancer; original scripts appear and fade outside reading surfaces, controls remain clear, and reduced motion is static.
FL-147.observed: Wizard and Technomancer original generated scripts reserve flex space in module chrome, clear of attunement and controls. Mount animations have one iteration; Wizard hover reveal has one iteration; reduced motion reports animation none. Message content has animation none. Desktop, Stage, Sheet and narrow captures retained.

FL-148.label: Liquid, shiny, white chrome on borders, not on buttons.
FL-148.walk: Switch to Seraph Dressed; borders show liquid white chrome and buttons do not.
FL-148.observed: Liquid white gradient rims with excluded-center masks surround all fourteen modules, including Farm, Roots and Palace. Per-module final captures and before/all-module-rims.json retained. Ordinary button surfaces do not use the rim material. Three-dimensional content quality is M3VL scope; empty or costly scene rendering is not claimed as new proof here.

FL-170.label: A fresh reinstall that reconnects to existing files and auto-finds the cloud palace.
FL-170.walk: Reinstall on the same machine and run the start command; it finds the existing cloud Palace and the old threads without being told where they are.
FL-170.observed: Public 0.1.27 reinstall restored the disposable identity and conversation. The new 0.1.28 registry-wheel restoration remains pending publication.

FL-186.label: Build on Pydantic AI in a way that lets us modify and extend without waiting on them, passing features back and forth with their library.
FL-186.walk: Upgrade the Pydantic AI dependency; the Harness's own additions keep working and the new upstream features are usable.
FL-186.observed: No Pydantic AI upgrade was made or walked; only the lockstep Memory version changed. Existing tests pass but do not prove a new upstream upgrade.

FL-190.label: The Harness can use skills and has the best and most common tools available, compiled from a list.
FL-190.walk: Ask the agent to use a skill in a thread; it loads the skill and follows it.
FL-190.observed: No skill execution was requested in the disposable live thread; inventory is context only.

FL-192.label: Swappable seams: router, model policy with an off-switch, toolset as a unit, memory system.

FL-192.observed: No whole-toolset config replacement was exercised; this packet changes only brand assets and release metadata.
